name: Aquaculture & Fisheries

objectives.text: Identify common farm-raised fish and shellfish, such as tilapia, catfish, trout, and shrimp, and name the water environment each lives in
Describe the life cycle of a fish from egg to fry to fingerling to adult
Describe what fish need to survive in a tank or pond, including clean water, oxygen, food, and space
Compare farm-raised fish with wild-caught fish and explain where each type of seafood comes from
Explain how water temperature, pH, and dissolved oxygen affect fish health in an aquaculture system
Explain how the nitrogen cycle converts fish waste from ammonia to nitrite to nitrate through beneficial bacteria in an aquaculture system
Compare the major aquaculture production systems, including ponds, raceways, net pens, and recirculating systems, by their water use, space, and management needs
Measure temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and ammonia in an aquaculture system and compare the results to recommended ranges for the species raised
Apply external characteristics such as fin placement, body shape, scale type, and mouth position to identify aquatic species using a dichotomous key
Explain how oxygen saturation, pH, alkalinity, hardness, and nitrogen compounds interact to determine water quality in fish culture and summarize the methods used to test each
Calculate fish biomass, daily feeding rate, and feed conversion ratio from sampling and growth records kept in an aquaculture supervised agricultural experience
Analyze water chemistry and feeding data from an aquaculture system to diagnose a decline in fish growth or survival
Classify common diseases of farmed fish by cause and analyze observed symptoms to recommend a treatment or biosecurity practice
Describe how aquaponic systems link fish production with plant production and recommend whether an aquaponic system fits a producer's goals and resources
Evaluate the fish and macroinvertebrate species present in a pond or stream to assess the health of the aquatic ecosystem
Analyze wild-capture fishing methods and aquaculture practices for their environmental, economic, and social sustainability
Develop recommendations for the sustainable harvest of a fish population using size limits, creel limits, quotas, and seasons as tools of faithful stewardship
Evaluate hatchery practices and biotechnologies such as induced spawning, sex reversal, triploidy, and selective breeding for improving aquaculture production
Develop an enterprise budget for an aquaculture operation that estimates fingerling, feed, and energy costs, expected yield, and break-even price
Design a recirculating aquaculture system's stocking density, feeding plan, and water treatment components to optimize fish growth and water quality

changes: Kept all six existing objectives as real competencies, rewording a few for precision and expanding the grade 2 species list and grade 4 needs. Added a fish life cycle objective, a farmed versus wild seafood comparison, the nitrogen cycle, and a comparison of production systems to fill the elementary and middle grades. Added high school competencies the field expects: species identification with a dichotomous key, water chemistry and testing methods, biomass and feed conversion calculations for SAE records, fish disease diagnosis and biosecurity, aquaponics, ecosystem assessment from aquatic species, sustainability of capture and culture methods, sustainable harvest regulation, hatchery biotechnology, and enterprise budgeting. Mapped AFNR standards only to grade 9 to 12 objectives where they genuinely apply. Left careers, product processing, and companion animals to sibling sub-topics.
